subject: Science
stem: Household electrical wiring uses parallel circuits rather than series circuits mainly because in a parallel circuit:

options.option_text: Each appliance gets the same full voltage and can operate independently, even if one fails
All appliances must always be switched on together
Only one appliance can be used at any given time
The voltage across each appliance is much less than the source voltage

explanation: Parallel wiring lets each appliance receive full source voltage and operate independently — one appliance failing or being switched off doesn't affect the others, unlike a series circuit.

subject: Science

options.option_text: Passing electric current through a coil of wire wound around a soft iron core
Heating a permanent magnet until it melts
Simply placing two bar magnets side by side

explanation: An electromagnet's magnetism arises from current flowing through a coil around a soft iron core; the field can be turned on/off by controlling the current — unlike a permanent magnet.

subject: Science
stem: An electric fuse in household wiring is designed to:

options.option_text: Melt and break the circuit when current exceeds a safe limit, preventing fire/damage
Increase the current flowing to appliances
Permanently connect all appliances regardless of current
Convert AC current to DC current

explanation: A fuse contains a wire that melts and breaks the circuit if current exceeds a safe threshold, protecting wiring and appliances from overheating/fire — a critical safety device, not a current booster.
